reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

observed.facings.png: A 4x4 linked-pipe atlas on a checkerboard: a thin copper-brown tube with a dark outline and faint grey-green speckle, in straights, elbows with about a half-cell radius, tees and a cross. Every 3- and 4-way junction has a round riveted boss with a domed centre. Dead ends have a rounded cap with a dark banded collar. The isolated tile is a lone riveted boss. The background is transparent.
observed.south.png: The same atlas on white at higher resolution. The tube is the same width and colour throughout and has a lighter highlight stripe down its centre. The greenish oxidation flecks repeat at regular intervals along the straights. Bosses have about 8 small rivets round the rim. End caps have a wrapped dark collar, two or three bands, in front of a copper dome. Elbows are smooth and on the pipe axis. No dents or patches are visible.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the same atlas, same tiles, same rendering.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px/cell on a brown ground. A horizontal run starts with a left end cap, then a valve/faucet sprite, then a tee with its riveted boss and a vertical branch going south to an end cap, then a sprinkler head, then a smooth S of two elbows rising north-east to a straight that ends in a cap. A vanilla pawn is shown in a side panel. All the joins are continuous: no gaps, kinks or offsets, and the boss sits centred on the run axis. The pipe is thin next to the pawn.
observed.siblings.png: The checkerboard upper area is empty. The lower panel is the Industrial sibling: the same layout drawn as a thin grey steel pipe with small dark fittings. The Scrapper candidate has the same geometry and thickness class as this sibling.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same layout at 90 px/cell. It is continuous and aligned, the tee boss centred, the elbows smooth, and the caps attached to the ends of the run. The copper reads clearly. The speckled oxidation shows as a regular dashed pattern along the straights.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same layout at 48 px/cell. It still reads as a copper pipe with a junction boss and capped ends. The oxidation becomes faint periodic dashes, and the valve and sprinkler stay readable.

CAMERA.seen: The pipe is flat ground art drawn by Graphic_Linked (an engine limit, so top-down is correct here). The bosses are round and symmetric, which is right for a flat floor fitting. There is no side elevation.

BORE.seen: No open bore is visible anywhere. End caps close every dead end with a dome.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1/2 and scale, each straight meets the next cell on the same axis with no gap or offset. The elbows join tangentially, the tee boss is centred on both axes, and the caps are flush with the ends of the run.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each atlas tile's pipe stubs reach the cell edge on the side that has a neighbour, and nowhere else. The cap tiles stop inside the cell with a cap, and there are no stray connectors.

LAYERS.seen: The faucet and sprinkler draw over the pipe, the boss draws over the crossing tubes, and nothing is wrongly occluded.

ROTATIONS.seen: One atlas. Every tile uses the same tube width, colour band, boss and cap design.

SIGNATURE.seen: The working parts are all recognisable: a linked floor pipe with elbows, tees with junction bosses, and end caps. The salvage character is weak, though; see the finding.

MATERIAL.seen: It reads as copper tube with a specular highlight and some greenish oxidation, not as a flat coat of paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The pipe is thin and centred on the cell axis, and the stubs end at the cell edges. Nothing overflows.

ALPHA.seen: facings.png shows a clean transparent background, with no drop shadow or ground patch.

OURS.seen: This is custom copper art with bespoke bosses and caps. It is not vanilla's pipe or a known mod's pipe.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The owner's complaints about bad alignment and mismatched parts are fixed: no banding, the elbows are on the pipe axis, the tee boss is centred, and the caps are attached. Whether the art is still 'bad' is subjective. The pipe now looks coherent, though fairly clean for scrap.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px/cell (assembled_2) it is clearly a copper pipe with a junction boss and caps. At 32 px it will be a thin coppery line with a dot at junctions, which is acceptable for floor clutter.

findings.seen: The tube is smooth and of uniform width, with a clean centre highlight. The oxidation shows only as small regularly spaced grey-green flecks, and no dents are visible. Overall it reads as a fairly well-kept copper pipe, not salvage/junk-built.
findings.quote: one oxidised, verdigris-blotched, dented copper tube
findings.fix: The copper tube carries heavier, irregular verdigris blotches and dull, darker patina, with subtle dents shown as small shading breaks along the outline, so it reads as salvaged scrap while keeping its width and colour band uniform.

findings.seen: The flecks repeat at fixed intervals along every straight. At 90 and 48 px/cell they read as a regular dashed pattern, almost a printed stripe, rather than random corrosion.
findings.quote: the salvage character sits in the oxidation and in the fittings
findings.fix: The oxidation on the straight tile is laid out irregularly along its length, so that repeated cells join into an organic, non-periodic patina with no visible dash rhythm.

reply.needs_call_why: The geometry and alignment problems the owner named are fixed and the parts are coherent. The open question is whether he will find the copper still too clean for 'Scrapper'; round 1 was rejected as too pristine, and this still shows little dent or patch character.

request.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

edits.change: The copper tube carries broad, irregular verdigris blotches of varied size, in pale blue-green crusts over dull, darker brown-bronze patina, with dark oxide streaks. The blotches are uneven in size and spacing, with no regular dotted rhythm. The centre highlight is dulled and broken by corrosion.

Shallow dents are visible along the tube: three or four soft concave dimples per cell, drawn as small shading breaks and slight notches in the dark outline, each with a darker shadow side and a lighter rim. The tube width and colour band stay uniform and the connection width stays consistent at every cell edge.

Every 3-way and 4-way junction carries a round, symmetric boss of scrap plate. The plate is rust-brown with scratches and a worn, chipped edge. Its fasteners visibly mismatch: some dark iron bolts and some bright brass rivets, in different sizes, with a rust stain around each. The dead-end cap has a crude wire-wrapped solder collar with a lumpy solder blob.

invariants: Uniform tube width and one colour band along every straight cell, so no banding
Elbows bent on the pipe axis with radius half a cell, with no kink
Round symmetric boss at every 3- and 4-way junction, centred on the pipe axes
End caps attached on-axis at N/S/E/W, with no detached caps
Flat, low, thin ground-clutter profile (about 18 px of a 132 px cell), with couplings fully inside the cell and none hidden in the atlas padding
4x4 Graphic_Linked atlas layout, transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
The faucet and sprinkler head are existing art and stay unchanged
request.prompt:
RimWorld floor pipe sprite atlas (4x4 Graphic_Linked cells, each 132 px, transparent background), painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline. Subject: a salvaged, junk-built water pipe, drawn flat, low and thin (about 18 px of the 132 px cell) as ground clutter seen from above. Cells: straight runs (horizontal and vertical), elbows, tees, a cross and end caps, so neighbouring cells join up seamlessly.

Tube: one oxidised, weathered copper tube of uniform width and one colour band, identical along every straight cell so runs tile without banding. The surface is heavily corroded: broad, irregular verdigris blotches of varied size, in pale blue-green crusts over dull, darker brown-bronze patina, with dark oxide streaks. The blotches are uneven in size and spacing and form no regular dotted pattern. The centre highlight is dulled and broken by corrosion. Shallow dents show along the tube: three or four soft concave dimples per cell, drawn as small shading breaks and slight notches in the dark outline, each with a darker shadow side and a lighter rim. The tube keeps a consistent connection width at every cell edge so cells meet cleanly.

Elbows: bent smoothly on the pipe axis with radius half a cell, with the same patina, dents and width as the straights.

Junctions: every 3-way and 4-way junction has a round, symmetric boss of scrap plate centred on the pipe axes. The plate is rust-brown with scratches and a worn, chipped edge. Its fasteners visibly mismatch: some dark iron bolts and some bright brass rivets, in different sizes, with a rust stain around each.

End caps: on each dead end, a cap attached on the pipe axis, finished with a crude wire-wrapped solder collar with a lumpy solder blob, in the same corroded copper.

All fittings sit fully inside their cell, with the tube ends meeting the cell edges exactly on the axis.
